title: Client Partnership Review — Playbook & Deck Variants
doc_summary: Working stash of two complementary QBR deck variants (concise standard + expanded enterprise) plus an associated renewal tracking CSV header, discussion prompts, and an operational playbook. Intention: give CSMs a lightweight path for monthly/quarterly check-ins and a heavier, executive-ready path for renewal or upsell conversations. NOT final — contains placeholders and example language that each CSM should localize before sending to customers.
audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Renewal Specialists, Solutions Engineers, Account Execs for renewal meetings
use_cases: 15–30 min health check catch-ups using the Standard deck
45–60 min executive reviews before renewal using Enterprise deck
Renewal prep for deals within 3 months of term end
Post-migration check-ins after Private deployment rollouts
slide_outline_standard: Cover: Customer name, CSM, meeting date, objective
Top wins since last meeting: 3 bullets (outcome + owner)
Usage & cost digest: tokens, peak latency, notable anomalies
Support & incidents summary: trending bugs, outstanding SLAs
Actions & quick wins: 2–3 items with owners and ETA
slide_outline_enterprise: Cover + agenda with executive sponsors listed
Strategic outcomes + alignment to customer OKRs (2–3 lines)
Detailed adoption map: teams, endpoints, model versions in use
Performance & cost story: 90-day graphs and batch/quantization impact
Risk register: capacity, compliance, data residency items
Value realization: case studies + ROI calc (savings vs self-host)
Renewal & expansion options: pricing scenarios and timelines
Commitments: action owners, SLAs, follow-up cadence, success criteria
recommended_metrics: Monthly token consumption vs committed capacity
Cache hit rate / effective tokens saved
Model version drift: percent requests on pinned vs latest
playbook_steps: 1) Pre-meeting: run renewal risk query in SFDC/Jira; pull console perf snapshots
2) Tailor deck: swap customer examples, set 2–3 measurable goals aligned to customer OKRs
3) Internal sync: 20-min prep with solutions engineer to validate metrics and ask list
4) Run meeting: use Standard for health check; switch to Enterprise if renewal or exec present
5) Capture commitments: use tracker row template and assign owners live
6) Post-meeting: update renewal stage in CRM, create follow-up ticket, send shared slide PDF within 24 hours
7) 14-day checkpoint: confirm progress on owners' action items and update risk score
example_exec_summary:
Executive summary (to paste at top of Enterprise deck):
Objective: Validate ROI and secure renewal conversation by presenting realized value and a clear, low-friction path to commit to next term.
Key points: 1) 90-day reduction in per-token cost from batching + quantization; 2) two product-led wins (search ranking, document summarization) delivering measurable KPI improvements; 3) roadmap asks: dedicated throughput increase and compliance audit support.
Asks: Confirm renewal term window, identify procurement lead, sign off on pilot extension (if required).
discussion_prompts: What business metric improved most since our last review? How do we attribute that change to Redwood features?
Are there upcoming product or regulatory initiatives that will change ML workload patterns?
If we had an additional 20% throughput, where would you apply it?
What would make renewal a 'no-brainer' for your procurement team?
common_objections_and_responses: Objection: 'Costs spiked last month' — Response: show token breakdown, demonstrate cache hit improvements and propose short-term rate-limited burst to smooth spikes
Objection: 'We need on-prem due to compliance' — Response: outline Redwood Private checklist, timeline estimate, and security contacts
Objection: 'Latency is unpredictable' — Response: present p50/p95 comparisons across regions and propose routing fallback + canary policy
notes_to_csm: Quick tips: personalize the opening 90 seconds, use the 1-slide health snapshot to control narrative, avoid drowning execs in raw token charts (use callouts). For enterprise decks, include a one-page ROI appendix. Keep language measurable and link to the specific console dashboards in the follow-up email.
